value.body: Plans and tracks how goods move from suppliers to warehouses and on to customers — booking transport, coordinating dispatches, chasing delays and keeping shipment records. Coordinators work at logistics and courier companies, freight forwarders, e-commerce firms, manufacturers and retailers. A day is spent on calls and messages with transporters, warehouses and customers, and on updating tracking systems.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: Supply-chain diplomas are a common add-on

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, ERP, warehouse and transport management software

items.label: Key documents
items.value: E-way bill, invoice, lorry receipt; shipping bill and bill of lading for exports

items.label: Logistics cost in India
items.source: NCAER study for DPIIT, Assessment of Logistics Cost in India (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers start as logistics or operations executives at transporters, warehouses, e-commerce hubs or freight forwarders, often through campus or walk-in hiring. Excel skills, comfort on the phone and basic knowledge of GST e-way bills help. Certificates from the Logistics Sector Skill Council or a supply-chain diploma can add to a CV.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Documentation — e-way bills, invoices, export papers

value.title: At a glance
items: The work is fast-paced and can involve shifts, especially in e-commerce and warehousing.
Growth path: coordinator → supervisor → logistics or supply-chain manager.
Export-import logistics is a specialised branch with its own documentation.

value.title: Logistics cost as a share of GDP
value.note: A measure of the sector's size, not of jobs; older studies used other methods and gave higher figures.
value.source: NCAER study for DPIIT, Assessment of Logistics Cost in India (as reported)
